Wilderness at the Smokies Winter 2026 Review: A Family-Friendly Smoky Mountains Christmas Getaway

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 14:55
Instaread

Y’all know how much we love visiting the Smoky Mountains! It’s one of our favorite places to take the kids, and we’ve made so many wonderful family memories there over the years. From spending time outdoors and exploring the mountains to enjoying all the family-friendly attractions in Sevierville, Pigeon Forge and Gatlinburg, there’s always something new to do. But one of our favorite places to stay is Wilderness at the Smokies, especially during the winter!

During one of our previous years visiting the Smokies, we stayed at Wilderness at the Smokies three different times, and there’s a reason we kept going back! I love that it’s such a convenient resort for families, especially when you’re traveling with multiple kids. Between the spacious accommodations, indoor waterpark, restaurants and entertainment, there’s so much to do without ever leaving the property. And during the Christmas season, the resort adds even more festive activities that make it such a fun winter getaway!

Why We Love Staying at Wilderness at the Smokies with Kids

One of the biggest reasons I love Wilderness at the Smokies is how family-friendly the entire resort is. Traveling with three kids means I’m always looking for accommodations that give everyone enough room to spread out while still being convenient to all the activities. Wilderness offers a variety of room styles, including suites, larger accommodations and vacation-style lodging options. I especially appreciate having extra space when we’re staying for more than just a night or two.

We’ve stayed in one- and two-bedroom accommodations as well as villas, and the extra space has always made our trips so much easier. I love having a kitchen when we’re traveling as a family because it makes breakfast, snacks and downtime much more convenient. Some of the larger accommodations also offer laundry facilities and separate living spaces, which are especially helpful when you’re spending several days at the resort. And with so much entertainment right on the property, it’s easy to enjoy a full family vacation without having to plan something different every day!

Wild WaterDome Indoor Waterpark: The Best Part of a Winter Stay

One of my favorite things about visiting Wilderness at the Smokies during the winter is the indoor waterpark! Even when it’s freezing outside, the kids can spend hours swimming, going down water slides and enjoying all the attractions. The Wild WaterDome is open year-round, making it such a fun option for a winter family vacation. I love that you can enjoy a tropical-style waterpark experience without having to travel somewhere warm!

The waterpark has attractions for different ages, which is especially important when you’re traveling with kids who aren’t all the same height. During our previous visits, Grayson enjoyed the younger children’s play areas while Amelia and Leighton loved trying the bigger slides. And as the kids have gotten older, it’s been fun seeing them become tall enough to experience more of the attractions together. There’s something so special about finding a place where everyone can enjoy the same vacation while still having activities that fit their age and interests.

Our Favorite Indoor Waterpark Rides at Wilderness at the Smokies

Kaleidoscope Kavern Lazy River

The Kaleidoscope Kavern Lazy River is one of the most unique lazy rivers we’ve experienced! As you float through the tunnel, you’re surrounded by colorful lighting, music and beautiful visual effects. It’s such a fun experience, and the kids have always loved it. I especially love that it’s a more relaxing attraction you can enjoy together between some of the bigger water slides.

Ridge Runner Water Coaster

Ridge Runner is another one of our favorites! This indoor water coaster combines the excitement of a roller coaster with a water slide, complete with drops, uphill sections and colorful effects. Both of the girls were able to enjoy it during one of our earlier trips, and we had so much fun riding together. It’s definitely one of the attractions I’d recommend trying if your kids meet the height requirements!

Storm Chaser

If your family loves thrill rides, Storm Chaser is one you won’t want to miss! This slide sends riders down a dark tunnel before dropping into a giant funnel, and it’s such an exciting experience. I remember wanting to ride it over and over again during our visit. It’s a great option for older kids and adults who love something a little more adventurous.

Trail Twisters

Trail Twisters is another attraction we rode again and again! These tube slides are full of twists and turns, and they’re such a fun way to enjoy the waterpark together. I especially love that you can ride in a tube and experience the excitement without it being quite as intense as some of the bigger thrill rides. It’s a great one for families who love traditional water slides.

Runaway Canyon

Runaway Canyon is such a fun family raft ride! This attraction takes several riders through a series of tunnels and turns, making it a great option for families who want to enjoy a slide together. During one of our earlier trips, Grayson wasn’t quite tall enough to ride, but the girls had a blast. It’s one of those rides that makes you look forward to returning as your younger kids get a little bigger!

Washout Mountain and the Younger Kids’ Play Areas

One thing I especially appreciate about Wilderness at the Smokies is that the younger kids have plenty to do too! Washout Mountain offers interactive water features, slides and a giant tipping bucket that kids love. The resort also has shallower activity areas designed for smaller children. I love that younger siblings can enjoy their own waterpark adventures while older kids are trying the bigger attractions.

Wilderness Adventure Forest: Indoor Family Fun Beyond the Waterpark

As much as we love the waterpark, there’s so much more to do at Wilderness at the Smokies! One of our favorite places to visit after swimming is Wilderness Adventure Forest, the resort’s indoor family entertainment center. During our previous stay, we ended up visiting almost every evening because the kids loved it so much. It’s such a fun way to spend time together after a full day in the water!

Adventure Forest offers a variety of attractions, including an indoor suspended roller coaster, ropes course, laser tag, mini bowling, glow-in-the-dark miniature golf and arcade games. There are also newer experiences such as escape rooms and additional interactive attractions. I love that there’s something for different ages and interests, whether your kids enjoy physical challenges, games or a little friendly competition. Be sure to check the current attraction passes and any individual height requirements before visiting.

Winter Wonderland and Christmas Activities at Wilderness at the Smokies in 2026

One of the things that made our previous winter stay so memorable was all the Christmas fun happening around the resort! The decorations, ice skating, holiday activities and festive atmosphere made the entire trip even more special. We loved having the option to spend part of the day swimming indoors and then head outside for Christmas activities. It really was such a fun combination for the kids!

For the 2026 holiday season, Wilderness at the Smokies is bringing back several seasonal experiences, including outdoor ice skating, Santa appearances, Santa’s Workshop and Christmas storytimes. I love that families can enjoy the waterpark and holiday activities during the same trip. And with so much happening around Sevierville during the Christmas season, it’s a wonderful place to plan a festive family getaway!

Outdoor Ice Skating at Wilderness at the Smokies

Ice skating was one of our absolute favorite activities during our previous winter visit! The kids loved it so much, and we could have spent hours out on the rink. I especially loved the Christmas music, hot chocolate and festive atmosphere. It was such a fun change of pace from the indoor waterpark, and it made the trip even more memorable.

For the 2026–2027 season, Wilderness at the Smokies has announced that its outdoor ice rink will operate November 6–8, then daily November 13 through January 3, with an additional weekend January 8–10. The resort transforms part of its outdoor waterpark into a real ice-skating rink, and both overnight guests and the public can participate. Some accommodations and booking packages include skating, while others offer it as an add-on, so I recommend checking the details before your trip.

Santa’s Workshop and Santa Appearances

If you’re visiting during the Christmas season, be sure to check the schedule for Santa’s Workshop! This festive experience gives children opportunities to enjoy holiday activities and write letters to Santa. I love little activities like this because they make a family vacation even more special for younger kids. It’s such a sweet way to add a little Christmas magic to your stay!

The resort has also announced Santa appearances on select dates beginning November 27 and continuing through December. I recommend checking the official holiday calendar before booking because appearances are scheduled for specific days and times. If seeing Santa is one of your family’s priorities, it’s definitely worth planning your visit around those dates!

Story Time with Mrs. Claus

Another sweet holiday activity at Wilderness at the Smokies is Story Time with Mrs. Claus! The resort has scheduled Christmas-themed storytimes on select weekends during November and December 2026. I love that this gives younger children a chance to enjoy something a little quieter between all the waterpark excitement. It’s also such a fun opportunity to make the trip feel extra festive.

Reservations may be required for storytime, so be sure to check availability when booking your stay. I especially love activities like this for families traveling with younger children who still enjoy all the traditional Christmas experiences!

Shadrack’s Christmas Wonderland Light Show

One of the highlights of our previous winter trip was visiting the Christmas light display at Soaky Mountain Waterpark! The kids absolutely loved it, and it was one of their favorite parts of the entire vacation. There were so many beautiful lights synchronized to music, and it was such a fun way to spend an evening together. I love that you can enjoy a festive experience like this just a short distance from the resort!

For the 2026 holiday season, Shadrack’s Christmas Wonderland is scheduled to return to Soaky Mountain Waterpark from November 13, 2026 through January 3, 2027. This drive-through light show is such a fun addition to a Smoky Mountains Christmas getaway. You can also check for available combination packages that include ice skating and admission to the light display.

Where to Stay at Wilderness at the Smokies with Kids

Choosing the right room can make such a difference when you’re traveling with children! One thing I love about Wilderness at the Smokies is that there are accommodations for different family sizes and vacation styles. Whether you’re planning a quick weekend trip or staying for several days, there are options that give families more space than a traditional hotel room. And when you’re traveling with three kids, I think having a little extra room makes the entire trip more enjoyable.

We especially love accommodations with separate bedrooms, a kitchen and a living area where everyone can relax. Having a place to prepare breakfast or snacks is so convenient, and I love not having to eat every single meal at a restaurant. If you’re traveling with grandparents or another family, the larger villas and multi-bedroom accommodations are worth considering. Just be sure to compare the location, amenities and waterpark access included with each room type before booking.

Dining and Family-Friendly Amenities at the Resort

Another reason I love staying at Wilderness at the Smokies is how convenient everything is once you’re there. Between the waterpark, restaurants, coffee shops, sweet treats and entertainment, you can easily spend several days on the property. I especially appreciate that after a long day of swimming, we don’t necessarily have to get everyone dressed and drive somewhere else for dinner. Sometimes being able to stay right at the resort is exactly what we need!

There are several dining options throughout the property, along with places to grab coffee, snacks and desserts. And depending on your accommodations, you may also have the option to prepare some of your own meals. I love having that flexibility when traveling with kids because it makes it easier to plan around everyone’s schedules and preferences.

Tips for Visiting Wilderness at the Smokies During Winter

If you’re planning a winter trip, I definitely recommend checking the holiday activity calendar before choosing your dates. Some Christmas events are offered only on select days, and certain activities may require advance reservations or additional tickets. It’s also a good idea to check the height requirements for water slides and Adventure Forest attractions so you know what your children will be able to enjoy. That can make planning your days much easier!

I also recommend packing swimsuits, comfortable clothes, warm layers and shoes suitable for outdoor winter activities. One of the things I love most about this resort is that you can spend the morning at the indoor waterpark and the evening ice skating or looking at Christmas lights. It’s such a fun mix of activities, but you’ll definitely want to be prepared for both indoor and outdoor adventures!

Is Wilderness at the Smokies Worth Visiting in Winter?

Absolutely! Wilderness at the Smokies has been one of our favorite family resorts in the Smoky Mountains for years, and I especially love visiting during the colder months. The indoor waterpark gives the kids plenty to do regardless of the weather, and all the additional entertainment makes it easy to enjoy a full family vacation. Add in the festive Christmas activities, and it’s such a wonderful option for a winter getaway!

I love that there’s something for everyone, from younger children who enjoy the splash areas and holiday storytimes to older kids who love the bigger water slides, arcade games and adventurous attractions. And for parents, having so many activities, dining options and accommodations in one place makes planning a trip so much easier.

Final Thoughts on a Winter Getaway to Wilderness at the Smokies

We’ve made so many wonderful memories at Wilderness at the Smokies, and I love that it’s a place we can continue enjoying as the kids grow. Between the indoor waterpark, spacious accommodations, family entertainment and Christmas activities, there’s so much to love about visiting during the winter. It’s one of those destinations where you can stay busy the entire trip or simply enjoy being together without having to plan every minute.

If you’re looking for a family-friendly Christmas getaway in the Smoky Mountains, I definitely recommend adding Wilderness at the Smokies to your list! Have you stayed here during the winter before? I’d love to hear which attractions and holiday activities your family enjoyed most!
